Traverse the graph of time unit relationships

Source: R/chronon_traverse.R
chronon_traverse.Rd

Walks out from a chronon through the time units it is related to by chronon_cardinality() methods, either to coarser or finer time units, accumulating a value along the way. This is a low-level building block for questions about how time units relate, such as "which coarser time units does a month nest within a fixed number of times?" or "which finer time units divide a day between 3 and 15 times?".

Usage

chronon_traverse(
  x,
  .f,
  .init,
  .until = function(acc, granule) FALSE,
  direction = c("coarser", "finer"),
  graph = c("fixed", "cardinality")
)

Arguments

x

A time granule to start from (e.g. cal_gregorian$month(1L)).

.f

A function function(acc, from, to) returning the accumulated value at time granule to, given the accumulated value acc at the adjacent time granule from it was reached from. from is x for the time units adjacent to x.

.init

The accumulated value at x.

.until

A function function(acc, granule) that returns TRUE to stop the traversal beyond granule. The granule is still included in the result, but time units only reachable through it are not visited.

direction

Walk to "coarser" time units (e.g. from months to years) or "finer" time units (e.g. from months to days).

graph

Which relationships to walk along: "fixed" uses only the constant relationships of chronon_cardinality_fixed() methods (e.g. 12 months in a year), while "cardinality" also includes context-dependent ones from chronon_cardinality() methods (e.g. days in a month).

Value

A list with one element for each time unit reached (excluding x's own time unit), named by its class and in breadth-first order. Each element is a list of granule, a single unit (n = 1L) granule of that time unit which inherits the calendar and properties (such as time zone) of x, and value, the accumulated value. A time unit with no registered relationships gives an empty list.

Details

The traversal is breadth-first, and when a time unit can be reached along several paths only the first (shortest) is followed. The accumulated value is a fold along that path, which suits values that compose along a path, such as fixed cardinalities, the path itself, or its length.

Context-dependent cardinalities don't compose along a path: the 29 days of February 2024 times the 3 months of a quarter is not the 91 days of the first quarter of 2024. Compute these from x itself, for example with function(acc, from, to) chronon_cardinality(x, to, at = at).

Examples

# Cumulative fixed cardinality of each coarser time unit
card_up <- function(acc, from, to) acc * chronon_cardinality_fixed(from, to)

# There are 3 months in a quarter, and 12 in a year
traversal <- chronon_traverse(cal_gregorian$month(1L), card_up, 1)
vapply(traversal, function(e) e$value, numeric(1L))
#>    mixtime::tu_year mixtime::tu_quarter 
#>                  12                   3 

# Coarser time units containing at most 15 hours
traversal <- chronon_traverse(
  cal_gregorian$hour(1L), card_up, 1,
  .until = function(acc, granule) acc >= 15
)
vapply(traversal, function(e) e$value, numeric(1L))
#> mixtime::tu_ampm  mixtime::tu_day 
#>               12               24 

# Finer time units that divide a day up to 15 times
card_down <- function(acc, from, to) acc * chronon_cardinality_fixed(to, from)
traversal <- chronon_traverse(
  cal_gregorian$day(1L), card_down, 1,
  .until = function(acc, granule) acc > 15,
  direction = "finer"
)
vapply(traversal, function(e) e$value, numeric(1L))
#> mixtime::tu_hour mixtime::tu_ampm 
#>               24                2 

# The path from minutes to each coarser time unit
traversal <- chronon_traverse(
  cal_gregorian$minute(1L),
  function(acc, from, to) c(acc, class(to)[[1L]]),
  .init = "mixtime::tu_minute"
)
vapply(traversal, function(e) paste(e$value, collapse = " > "), character(1L))
#>                                                             mixtime::tu_hour 
#>                                      "mixtime::tu_minute > mixtime::tu_hour" 
#>                                                             mixtime::tu_ampm 
#>                   "mixtime::tu_minute > mixtime::tu_hour > mixtime::tu_ampm" 
#>                                                              mixtime::tu_day 
#>                    "mixtime::tu_minute > mixtime::tu_hour > mixtime::tu_day" 
#>                                                             mixtime::tu_week 
#> "mixtime::tu_minute > mixtime::tu_hour > mixtime::tu_day > mixtime::tu_week"
